ai.description: This gecko reaches 60 mm snout-vent length. It is greyish-brown with dark dorsal blotches and a white venter. Key features include a depressed body, webbed toes, and a tail with enlarged tubercles.
ai.identificationRemarks: The most reliable diagnostic feature of *Hemidactylus prashadi* is the presence of a distinct, continuous white or pale vertebral stripe running along the center of its back.
ai.habitat: *Hemidactylus prashadi* inhabits moist deciduous and semi-evergreen forests of the Western Ghats, typically found on tree trunks at elevations between 500 and 1,200 meters.
ai.behavior: The Bombay Leaf-toed Gecko is primarily nocturnal, emerging at night to actively hunt insects on vertical surfaces like rock faces and tree trunks.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Hemidactylus prashadi* is oviparous, typically laying a single hard-shelled egg per clutch. Breeding occurs primarily during the monsoon season, from June to September.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Hemidactylus prashadi* is endemic to the Northern Western Ghats in Maharashtra, India, typically inhabiting rocky outcrops at elevations between 600 and 1,200 meters.
